New6,7 or exacerbated8 cases of ulcerative colitis have been reported in patients on interferon or peginterferon alfa treat- ment (with or without ribavirin). Treatment with interferon was usually stopped7,8 and symptoms tended to resolve or improve with appropriate therapy (such as mesalazine and/or corticoster- oids).6-8 Cases of ischaemic colitis associated with interferon or peginterferon alpha have been reported rarely.9 1. Excessive temporary loss of telogen hair causing moderate and reversible alopecia occurs in about 7 to 30% of patients on interferon or peginterferon alfa treatment. Alopecia areata1-3 and alopecia universalis4,5 have occasionally been reported; complete regrowth of the hair usually occurs on completing interferon treatment.
